title: Dependency ownership ledger and handoff protocol
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: Roadmap planning across Eng/Design/Security/Infra frequently stalls because ownership of cross-cutting dependencies is ambiguous, handoffs are ad-hoc, and status updates are noisy or delayed. This causes missed launch windows and last-minute scope changes for customer-impacting initiatives.

Goal: Create a lightweight, auditable 'Dependency Ownership Ledger' and a standardized 'Handoff Protocol' that live in Linear and are surfaced in planning docs and the Console signalboard. The ledger will capture an authoritative owner, secondary owner, current lifecycle state, expected handoff date, and triage path for all cross-team dependencies tied to a roadmap initiative. The handoff protocol defines triggering events, acceptance criteria for transfer, and a rollback/fallback plan.

Scope: Build the data model and column conventions in Linear + add a checklist template for handoffs; prototype a small automation that emails owners 7 days before expected handoff and adds a ‘handoff-ready’ checklist to the ticket; author PM playbook and run two pilots (Runtime team -> Infra; Console -> Design). Exclusions: full company-wide automation and analytics dashboard (follow-up work).
acceptance_criteria: Ledger fields added to Linear template and defaults populated for new cross-team dependencies
Handoff checklist template implemented and attached to tickets by PMs
Two pilot handoffs completed with documented retros and improvements
Automation validates owner exists and sends 7-day reminder notifications
SLO: reduce last-minute dependency clarifications in pilot initiatives by 60%
updates: 2025-01-12: Kickoff with Eng (Diego), Design (Sophie Kim), Security (Ravi Shah), Infra (Maya Liu). Agreed ledger fields: owner, secondary_owner, lifecycle_state, expected_handoff_date, acceptance_criteria, fallback_plan, related_artifacts.
2025-01-20: Linear template created (branch: pm/dependency-ledger). Shared with PMs in roadmap sync; initial feedback: include 'risk_score' and 'customer_impact' as visible badges.

2025-01-28: Prototype automation—GitHub Actions workflow that triggers on ticket creation to populate ledger fields and schedule notifications. PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/linear-automations/pull/54.
2025-02-03: Pilot pairings confirmed: Runtime -> Infra (feature: continuous batching opt-in) and Console -> Design (feature: dependency visualization). PMs assigned to both pilots.
2025-02-10: First pilot handoff completed (Runtime -> Infra). Retros: Handoff checklist adequate but missing 'quantitative success metric' field. Added to checklist.

2025-02-14: Design review of ledger UI copy. SOP draft posted to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pm/dependency-ledger (internal). Next: enable 7-day reminders and create rollout plan for Q2.
Blockers: Need SSO permission to add automation webhook in Linear; Security requested brief review of webhook auth model (see SEC-22).
comments: Sophie Kim (Design) 2025-01-12: Recommend a compact view for execs (owner + ETA + risk) and an expanded view for doers with checklist and artifacts.
Ravi Shah (Security) 2025-01-20: Need to ensure automation tokens rotated and least-privilege webhooks used. Will do a light review after pilot.
Diego Morales (PM) 2025-01-28: Github automation PR added — requires infra approval to create service account. Tagging ENG ops.
Maya Liu (Infra) 2025-02-01: We can run the automation from a shared infra service account. Need scoped permissions from Security.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: keeping ledger minimal vs. collecting richer telemetry. Decision: start minimal (8 fields) to lower friction; extend after 2 pilots.
Fallback plan: if owner becomes unresponsive within 48 hours of a blocker, automatic escalation to the team lead and auto-assign secondary_owner.
Longer-term: expose ledger to Console signalboard and add a dependency freshness metric for quarterly OKRs (separate epics).
